authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from a measured run through the production entry (ASTEngine.parseFile) and checked line by line against the fixture source. First transcription guessed the line numbers and put `vpc.value.id` in the expected set; re-read against the numbered source, `vpc.value.id` is the block's OWN loop local and belongs in the FORBID set, which is the point of the fixture. `dynamic.vpc#2` was a bad guess on the first pass: the two `dynamic "vpc"` blocks are in different resources, so per-parent disambiguation correctly leaves both named `dynamic.vpc`.
rationale: H7b (reviews/hcl/master-review.md) — the sibling-scoping half of the dynamic-iterator defect, and the one the first fix got wrong in the OTHER direction. Terraform binds a dynamic block's loop local to that block; it is not a property of the enclosing resource. Binding the name for the whole enclosing subtree leaks sideways, which the corpus measured as 247 lost references over 9,079 files, 165 of them `assume_role.value` in tf-aws-components' provider files: a resource carrying `dynamic "assume_role"` and, later, `dynamic "vpc"` had its `vpc.*` reads silenced by the unrelated first block. The fix counts how many ENCLOSING dynamic blocks bind each name, so a name is suppressed only while such a block is still open — which still lets a local reach its own nested `content`, and still lets a nested dynamic shadow an outer one. This is the exact shape that regressed, so it is pinned rather than described. The last block added to the fixture is the regression case in its purest form: a `dynamic "vpc"` block and, in the SAME resource but OUTSIDE that block, a read of `vpc.main` — a real resource whose type happens to be `vpc`. Scoping the local to the block's own body is what keeps that read; the subtree-wide binding of the first fix is what lost it. Without this block the fixture passed under BOTH scopings, which is exactly why it is here: the hcl/dynamic-local-escapes-to-sibling mutant survived until this line existed.
